question: Should OpenClaw adopt this five-part localization RFC and its fail-closed repository-wide coverage gate as a core product and CI policy, rather than treating this cumulative draft as an independently landable change?
rationale: The patch creates a new cross-surface localization governance model and required check behavior; repository policy requires maintainer intent for broad product, config, and compatibility-sensitive direction.

options.title: Sponsor and sequence the RFC
options.body: Approve the localization direction, land the prerequisite foundation PRs first, and rebase this slice as the focused governance/checks change.

options.title: Narrow to guidance first
options.body: Keep the contributor documentation and inventory discussion, but defer required promotion blockers until maintainers define the rollout contract.

options.title: Decline core governance scope
options.body: Close or redirect the RFC if a repository-wide localization runtime and enforcement gate should not become a core responsibility.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and sequence the RFC
recommendation.body: Approve the localization direction, land the prerequisite foundation PRs first, and rebase this slice as the focused governance/checks change.

likelyOwner.reason: The author coordinates the active five-part proposal and can supply the RFC context, although final product acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
